diagnostics.message:
[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The EventBridge target can begin delivering scheduled events before the Lambda resource-based permission is installed. Make the target wait for the permission so invocations are not rejected during creation.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The EventBridge target can begin invoking the scale-down Lambda as soon as it is installed, but it does not wait for the matching Lambda permission. Order target creation after the permission to avoid invocation failures during setup.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The EventBridge target can become active before the Lambda resource-based invoke permission is installed. Ensure the permission exists before attaching the target to avoid scheduled invocations being denied during deployment.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`aws_cloudwatch_event_target.scale_down` may be created, and the scheduled rule may fire, before `aws_lambda_permission.scale_down` grants EventBridge permission to invoke the function; the target should be ordered after the invoke permission.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
aws_cloudwatch_event_target.scale_down can invoke aws_lambda_function.scale_down only if aws_lambda_permission.scale_down (principal events.amazonaws.com) exists first. The target references the rule and the function ARN but not the permission, so Terraform may create/enable the rule's target before the resource-based invoke policy is in place, causing invocations to fail until the permission propagates. Add an explicit dependency on aws_lambda_permission.scale_down.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
aws_cloudwatch_event_target.scale_down points the scheduled rule at the scale_down Lambda, but it does not depend on aws_lambda_permission.scale_down, the resource-based policy that authorizes events.amazonaws.com to invoke the function. Because the rule is enabled and fires on its schedule, once the rule+target exist an invocation can occur before the Lambda permission is created, causing "Resource-based policy does not allow this action" failures. The event target should be created after the Lambda permission.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The EventBridge target can begin delivering scheduled events before the Lambda resource-based permission is installed. Make the target wait for the permission so invocations are not rejected during creation.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The EventBridge target can begin invoking the SSM housekeeper Lambda as soon as it is installed, but it does not wait for the matching Lambda permission. Order target creation after the permission to avoid invocation failures during setup.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The EventBridge target can be created and enabled before the Lambda invoke permission is installed, so scheduled invocations may be rejected during deployment. Make the target depend on the matching permission.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`aws_cloudwatch_event_target.ssm_housekeeper` may be created, and the scheduled rule may fire, before `aws_lambda_permission.ssm_housekeeper` grants EventBridge permission to invoke the function; the target should be ordered after the invoke permission.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
aws_cloudwatch_event_target.ssm_housekeeper can invoke aws_lambda_function.ssm_housekeeper only if aws_lambda_permission.ssm_housekeeper (principal events.amazonaws.com) exists first. The target references the rule and the function ARN but not the permission, so EventBridge may register the target before the invoke policy exists, causing scheduled invocations to fail. Add an explicit dependency on aws_lambda_permission.ssm_housekeeper.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
aws_cloudwatch_event_target.ssm_housekeeper points the scheduled rule at the ssm_housekeeper Lambda, but it does not depend on aws_lambda_permission.ssm_housekeeper, the resource-based policy that authorizes events.amazonaws.com to invoke the function. Once the rule+target exist (and the rule is ENABLED), an invocation can fire before the Lambda permission is created, causing invocation AccessDenied failures. The event target should be created after the Lambda permission.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The enabled schedule can invoke the pool Lambda before Scheduler's invocation policy is installed on its execution role. Make the schedule wait for the policy to prevent early invocations from being denied.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The scheduled pool Lambda can be invoked before its scheduler role has the policy granting lambda:InvokeFunction. Ensure the role policy is attached before creating the schedule.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The EventBridge Scheduler schedule may become active before the scheduler role's Lambda-invoke policy is attached, causing scheduled invocations to be denied. Order schedule creation after the policy resource.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`module.pool:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool` may be enabled and fire before `module.pool:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler` grants the scheduler execution role `lambda:InvokeFunction`; the schedule should be ordered after that role policy.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
aws_scheduler_schedule.pool uses aws_iam_role.scheduler as its target role_arn to invoke aws_lambda_function.pool, but the role only gains lambda:InvokeFunction via aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler. The schedule references the role ARN but not the policy, so a scheduled invocation may fire before the execution role has the invoke permission attached, causing the first runs to fail. Add an explicit dependency on aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
aws_scheduler_schedule.pool targets the pool Lambda using aws_iam_role.scheduler.arn, but it does not depend on aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler, which is what actually grants the scheduler execution role lambda:InvokeFunction on the pool Lambda. The role's trust policy (assume role) may exist before its permission policy is attached, so the schedule can be created and fire while the role still lacks invoke permission, causing AccessDenied at invocation. The schedule should be created after the scheduler role policy.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The SQS event source mapping can begin polling and invoking the scale-up Lambda before its execution-role policy grants the required queue permissions. Create the mapping only after the policy is attached.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The scale-up Lambda can be invoked by the SQS event source mapping after it is created, but its execution role's scale-up policy is unordered. Ensure the policy is attached before enabling the mapping to avoid early invocations without required permissions.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up` can be created before `aws_iam_role_policy.scale_up` grants the Lambda execution role permission to receive/delete messages from the SQS queue; event source mapping creation can fail until that role policy exists.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up is created referencing the scale_up Lambda's ARN, but not the IAM role policy that grants the function's execution role permission to poll the SQS build queue (sqs:ReceiveMessage/DeleteMessage/GetQueueAttributes). AWS validates the execution role's SQS permissions at CreateEventSourceMapping time and fails with "The provided execution role does not have permissions to call ReceiveMessage on SQS" if aws_iam_role_policy.scale_up hasn't been created/attached yet. The event source mapping currently only transitively depends on the role (via the lambda), not on the role policy that actually grants the receive permission.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`module.job_retry:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.job_retry` can be created before `module.job_retry:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.job_retry` grants the Lambda execution role permission to receive/delete messages from the retry SQS queue; event source mapping creation can fail until that role policy exists.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.job_retry references the job-retry Lambda and the SQS retry queue, but not aws_iam_role_policy.job_retry, which is what grants the Lambda execution role permission to consume the retry queue (sqs:ReceiveMessage/DeleteMessage/etc.). AWS validates the execution role's SQS permissions when the event source mapping is created, so the create can fail if the role policy isn't in place yet. The mapping depends on the lambda output and queue, but both siblings can be created before the role policy.

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
The scale-up lambda embeds the job-retry check queue URL in its environment: `JOB_RETRY_CONFIG = jsonencode(local.job_retry_config)` where `local.job_retry_config` reads `module.job_retry[0].job_retry_check_queue.url`. The dependency graph shows no edge from :resource.aws_lambda_function.scale_up to module.job_retry:output.job_retry_check_queue (the reference is hidden behind a local), so the function could be created before the job-retry queue exists and would not be updated when the queue URL changes. Add `depends_on = [module.job_retry]` (or otherwise surface the queue reference in a direct attribute) on the scale-up lambda.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
`:resource.aws_lambda_function.scale_up` sets the `JOB_RETRY_CONFIG` environment variable from `local.job_retry_config`, which embeds `module.job_retry[0].job_retry_check_queue.url`, but the function has no dependency on `module.job_retry:output.job_retry_check_queue` (only the sibling `aws_iam_role_policy.job_retry_sqs_publish` depends on it). The scale-up function can therefore be created before the job-retry check queue exists, pointing at a queue URL that is not yet provisioned.
